item.title: Okaloosa County Suspends License Plate Camera Program
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Okaloosa County Sheriff's Office has announced it will remove and suspend its Automatic License Plate Recognition camera program, commonly known as Flock cameras, according to WKRG News 5. The decision marks a significant shift in the agency's approach to traffic and criminal investigations. Flock cameras use automated technology to capture…
item.content:encoded:
The Okaloosa County Sheriff's Office has announced it will remove and suspend its Automatic License Plate Recognition camera program, commonly known as Flock cameras, according to WKRG News 5.

The decision marks a significant shift in the agency's approach to traffic and criminal investigations. Flock cameras use automated technology to capture and catalog vehicle license plates, helping law enforcement identify stolen vehicles and track suspects.

The sheriff's office has not yet released details about the timing of the removal or the specific reasons behind the decision to suspend the program. The announcement comes as similar license plate reader programs across the country face ongoing scrutiny over privacy concerns and civil liberties questions.

This suspension affects Okaloosa County, which neighbors Santa Rosa County to the east. Residents and businesses in the region may see changes in how local law enforcement handles certain investigative operations that previously relied on the camera network.

item.content:encoded:
A pawn shop in nearby Daphne, Alabama is launching a program to provide temporary firearm storage for veterans, first responders, and others facing personal crises, according to WKRG News 5.

The initiative gives individuals experiencing difficult periods a safe way to secure their firearms away from home, removing access during vulnerable moments. The service is being offered at no cost to participants.

Programs like this one have gained traction across the country as communities seek practical approaches to suicide prevention and crisis intervention. The Daphne business is joining a broader network of gun owners and retailers working to expand safe storage options.

Details on how to access the service or which individuals qualify are available directly through the pawn shop. The program reflects growing recognition that temporary firearm removal during mental health crises can be a life-saving measure.

item.title: OKALOOSA COUNTY SHERIFF REMOVING LICENSE PLATE CAMERAS
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: The Okaloosa County Sheriff’s Office says it will begin removing and suspending its automated license plate reader camera program following a new Florida Department of Transportation memorandum. The memo revokes permits allowing local law enforcement agencies to place the cameras within state road rights-of-way, citing concerns about rapid…
item.content:encoded: The Okaloosa County Sheriff’s Office says it will begin removing and suspending its automated license plate reader camera program following a new Florida Department of Transportation memorandum. The memo revokes permits allowing local law enforcement agencies to place the cameras within state road rights-of-way, citing concerns about rapid deployment, data privacy and surveillance. Agencies have 30 days to remove affected cameras. Sheriff Aden says the technology has been valuable in solving crimes and protecting lives, but the department will comply with the new directive. The sheriff’s office will also remove its remaining cameras on county rights-of-way.

item.title: FDOT weighing options for safety improvements at Highway 29 and Barrineau Park Road
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: The Florida Department of Transportation is considering two options to improve safety at Highway 29 and Barrineau Park Road. One would install a traditional traffic signal while keeping the intersection largely as it is. The other would create a restricted crossing U-turn, or RCUT, using a concrete barrier to prevent Highway 196 traffic from…
item.content:encoded: The Florida Department of Transportation is considering two options to improve safety at Highway 29 and Barrineau Park Road. One would install a traditional traffic signal while keeping the intersection largely as it is. The other would create a restricted crossing U-turn, or RCUT, using a concrete barrier to prevent Highway 196 traffic from crossing Highway 29 directly. Drivers would instead turn right and use a designated U-turn. Both designs are 60-percent complete, with final design expected in early 2027 and construction planned for 2027 and 2028. FDOT will hold a public meeting September 15th from 5:30 to 6:30 p.m. at Victory Assembly of God, with a virtual option also available.

item.content:encoded: The History Museum of Mobile is preparing to launch a new exhibit this fall that will explore the city's role during America's Gilded Age. According to WKRG News 5, the 'Mobile in the Gilded Age' exhibit opens in October and will offer visitors a look at how the city developed during one of America's most transformative economic periods. The Gilded Age, roughly spanning the 1870s through early 1900s, saw rapid industrialization and wealth creation across the nation, and Mobile played its own significant role during that era. The museum, a key cultural institution in downtown Mobile, regularly features exhibits examining the region's rich history and economic development. Details about specific artifacts, artifacts on display, and the full scope of the exhibit are expected to be released as the October opening approaches.

item.content:encoded:
The Mobile Drug Education Council is planning a special concert to mark Overdose Awareness Day and kick off Recovery Month, according to a news release. The event will feature pianist John McAndrew and aims to create a night focused on music, hope, and remembrance for those affected by substance use disorder.

Overdose Awareness Day is observed annually to honor lives lost to overdose and raise awareness about the ongoing addiction crisis affecting communities across the region.

For residents in the Pensacola area struggling with substance abuse or seeking recovery resources, local support services and addiction treatment providers are available through Escambia and Santa Rosa County health departments.

item.content:encoded: The shower activity we had the past few days was due to a low pressure system just offshore, is now expected to become Tropical Storm Edouard later today. The system is currently south of Louisiana and is forecast to reach the coast of southwest Louisiana/upper Texas by tomorrow evening as a tropical storm. Those along the SW Louisiana and upper Texas coastline are currently under a Tropical Storm warning. Tropical storm force winds, coastal flooding, and heavy rain is expected as the system moves onshore.

item.content:encoded: Pensacola State College has a new leader in the pipeline. The District Board of Trustees' Search Committee has recommended J. Alex Kelly as the sole finalist for College president. Kelly currently serves as Florida's Secretary of Commerce, overseeing the state's economic development and workforce programs. Board Chair Zack Smith says Kelly showed a clear vision for the College's future throughout the search. Kelly will visit campus in late September to meet with students, faculty and the community before trustees vote on his appointment.
